title: Is it possible to have a player death animation when health reaches 0, but before game over screen...

posts.author: GrimRose
posts.body:
I wanted to implement simple enemies that chase/attack the player and either do damage to the player character's health or mind.
When the player reaches 0 Health (HP) or 0 Mind (MP) stat it triggers the game over. I was wondering if it would be possible to change the player character sprite to have the character collapse/fall to the ground before triggering the game over screen.
I would also like to possibly include an animated death scene for specific unique game overs.  I want to have the animation play when health reaches 0, but before triggering a game over.

How are you implementing it?
What your title implies is what I think most people would think when you say "health reaches 0" - that is to say, the default turn based system.
However you text implies you have something non-standard.
We need to know how you are implementing it in order to tell you how to make it work.
I've never used HP damage on the map, so I can't say with certainty whether running out of HP on the map will automatically trigger the game over screen.
If that is the case, a simple evented solution would be to track a variable instead of the default HP stat, but not knowing how this mechanic works or what your game is, my solution may vary from slightly janky to Jeff Jankos.
You can also use a conditional on the event to check player HP to trigger anything you want, such as checking if the HP is equal to or less than 0, and then run video files or sprite changes.

So, I assume that you are using the default Change HP events commands to deal the "damage" to the character, right?
By default, whenever the HP of all party members reaches 0, a Game Over is triggered. So, you either need a workaround or a plugin.
If you want a workaround, then the simplest way to do this is to disregard the 0 HP and just have the Game Over common event happen when the character reaches 1 HP. Not ideal, but it works and if you adjust the UI for it accordingly, the player probably won't even notice. The Change HP event command  has an "Allow Knockout" option you can tick to make the damage from it lethal. If you don't tick it, then the damage can't reduce the character's HP below 1. So, it's quick and easy, just make all the damage the protagonist takes non-lethal and trigger the Common Event when they are at 1 HP.
If you want a plugin, then RPG Maker MZ has one included by default, but not MV. So, after a casual search for one, maybe this one will work for you:
https://manugamingcreations.itch.io/rpg-maker-plugin-game-over-common-event

So I don't know if it's possible to close this thread, but I think I found a solution for what I'm looking for.
In the event I use the Change Hp/MP event command, but also have a variable that changes the same as the Hp/Mp. One variable for Mind and the other for Health. I already have the event check for if the variable is lower than 5, as it triggers a common event when the character's sanity slips below 5.
The plan is to do a conditional branch that checks if the Health/Mind variable is below 1, right after changing the variable, but before changing the HP. If variable is indeed below 1 then I will have it trigger a common event (death sequence) and then change the Hp/Mp to 0 to trigger the game over screen.
I'm currently working on the death animation and will test it out when I've finished the death sprite animation.

Well, if you are doing it like this, then just disabling "Allow Knockout" on all Change HP event commands and triggering the Game Over common event on 1 HP seems much simpler, no? Unless your HP values are low enough that 1 HP matters a lot.
And you don't need to reduce HP to 0. You can trigger a Game Over straight up via an event command. In fact, you should probably do that anyway, since you already have a Game Over animation common event and doing straight up via an event command has less chance of bugs. With the way you've described it, you are triggering the game over event before the actual HP reaches 0, so there's no real difference anyway.
What you described should work, but seems unnecessarily complex and might bug out if you change something later or decide to add some plugin that affects this.
Glad you found a solution either way!
